### Making a Heat Map

**Composition Across 2 Decades**

- The OPIHI dataset records 7108 quadrats at 41 sites across 13 survey years, scored by point-intercept
- @fig-cover-by-top-taxa shows the twelve most abundant taxa, as mean percent cover per quadrat, pooled across every site in each year.
- Two taxa dominate throughout:
  - `Turf algae` account for 30.6% of all recorded cover and `Padina` for 16.1%
  - `Crustose coralline` algae are a distant third at 7.0%, and the remaining 204 taxa divide what is left

```{r Load Libraries}
#| warning = FALSE
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)
library(stringi)
library(plotly)
```

```{r Top 12 Abundace Heat Map}
#| label: fig-cover-by-top-taxa
#| fig-cap: "Mean percent cover per quadrat by taxon and survey year, for the most abundant taxa within the selected functional group. Use the dropdown to switch groups."

raw <- read_csv(here("Outputs", "clean_master_sheet_percent_cover.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)

# The below below columns together identify ONE quadrat observation
# Verified against the data: these give 7,108 units, every one summing to exactly 100%

quad_keys <- c("date", "site_key", "transect_id", "quadrat_id", "position")

master <- read_csv(here("Outputs", "clean_master_sheet_percent_cover.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    date = if (inherits(date, "Date")) date
           else as_date(parse_date_time(date, orders = c("mdy", "ymd"))),
    year = year(date)
  )

stopifnot(!any(is.na(master$year))) 

# Rank taxa by total cover across the whole dataset. Summing raw percent_cover
# Absent rows contribute nothing to a sum, so the ranking is unaffected. It is only MEANS that need the zeros made explicit.

top_taxa <- master |>
  group_by(taxon_key) |>
  summarise(total = sum(percent_cover, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total, n = 12) |>
  pull(taxon_key)

taxon_year <- master |>
  filter(taxon_key %in% top_taxa) |>
  select(all_of(quad_keys), year, taxon_key, percent_cover) |>
  # Complete within the filtered set - absences become zeros
  # 23,356 rows over 7,108 quadrats is ~3.3 taxa per quadrat out of 207.
  # Without it, mean(percent_cover) = "mean cover WHEN PRESENT",
  # For patchy species is a completely different result
  # nesting() keeps only the quadrat x year combinations that really exist,
  # rather than crossing every column with every other
  complete(nesting(!!!syms(c(quad_keys, "year"))), taxon_key,
           fill = list(percent_cover = 0)) |>
  group_by(year, taxon_key) |>
  summarise(
    mean_cover = mean(percent_cover),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Order taxa by overall abundance so the axis isn't alphabetical
  # Averages each taxon's yearly means to get one sort value per taxon
  mutate(taxon_key = fct_reorder(taxon_key, mean_cover, .fun = mean))

cover_by_taxa_plot <- ggplot(taxon_year, aes(x = factor(year), y = taxon_key, fill = mean_cover)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # Sequential single hue: lightness rises monotonically with cover, so the
  # reader can tell which end means "more"
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1,
                       labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%"),
                       name = "Mean\ncover") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    title = "Turf and Padina dominate Hawaiʻi's intertidal across two decades",
    subtitle = "Mean percent cover per quadrat, pooled across all sites. Top 12 taxa by abundance.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = "Point-intercept data, 7,108 quadrats at 41 sites. Quadrats with absences counted as zero\nYears 2009-2015 and 2021-2023 not surveyed."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(), # gridlines add nothing behind tiles
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey45", size = 7.5)
  )

cover_by_taxa_plot
```

#### Computing Means for Composition Heat Map

- How the means are computed: taxon absent from a quadrat generates no row in the raw data, so the records average about 3.3 taxa per quadrat out of 207 possible.
- Taking a mean over the rows as given would answer “mean cover when present”, which for a patchy species is a very different number from mean cover
- Every figure here therefore completes the taxon-by-quadrat grid first, so an absence is counted as a genuine zero

#### Gaps in Surveys

- No surveys were carried out between 2009 and 2015, or 2021 and 2023
- Axis categorical, so years are omitted rather than left as empty columns

```{r Functional Group Classification}
# case_when() evals top to bottom, stops at the first TRUE
# ORDER IS THE LOGIC here
# Every branch below sits where it does for a reason

draft_groups <- master |>
  distinct(taxon_key) |>
  mutate(functional_group = case_when(

    # Turf first, as its own category - it alone is 30.6% of all cover
    # Kept separated so that algal composition is clearer
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("\\bturf\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Turf",

    # \\bsand\\b so it cannot match inside "Cellana sandwicensis"
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("bare rock|^rock$|\\bsand\\b|rubble|pebble|limestone|^hole$|basalt|sediment", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Substrate",

    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("cyanobacteria|lyngbya|symploca", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Cyanobacteria",

    # Crustose coralline algae -> Algae. Must sit ABOVE the coral
    # Otherwise "Coralline" gets caught by "coral"
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("crustose coralline", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Algae",

    # Same reasoning "Articallate Corraline" might be caught in coral
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("articulated coralline|^jania|galaxaura|halimeda|bornetella|neomeris|liagora|dichotomaria", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Calcified algae",

    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("coral|porites|montipora|pocillopora", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Coral",

    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("echinometra|urchin|colobocentrotus|cucumber|actinopyga|holothuria|sea star", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Echinoderm",

    # cellana, limpet and opihi live here - they are gastropods
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("snail|nerita|littorar|littorina|siphonaria|dendropoma|isognomon|thylacodes|morula|brachidontes|haminoea|serpulorbis|mussel|cellana|limpet|opihi", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Mollusc",

    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("barnacle|crab|grapsus|polychaete|anthopleura|anemone|hydroid|pennaria|sponge", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Other invertebrate",

    # \\bcrust\\b with boundaries, so "tenuicrustatus" not caught
    str_detect(taxon_key, regex("unknown|\\bcrust\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Unresolved",

    # Catch-all. Most of the 207 taxa are algae
    # The majority case and goes last by design
    TRUE ~ "Algae"
  ))

count(draft_groups, functional_group, sort = TRUE)


# Export WITH total abundance, so review effort goes to the taxa that
# actually move the figures rather than down the alphabet 
draft_groups |>
  left_join(master |> group_by(taxon_key) |>
              summarise(total = sum(percent_cover, na.rm = TRUE)), by = "taxon_key") |>
  arrange(functional_group, desc(total)) |>
  write_csv(here("Outputs", "functional_groups_to_review.csv"))
```

### Grouping and Plotting Functions

1.  `group_summary()` takes the master sheet and a group name and returns one row per taxon per year. It does three things in a fixed order: identify the most abundant taxa within that group, complete the taxon-by-quadrat grid so absences become zeros, then average. The order matters more than it looks.

2.  `group_heatmap()` takes the same arguments and returns a ggplot. Keeping it separate from `group_summary()` means the summarized numbers can be inspected, exported or tested without drawing anything, and the same summary feeds both the static figure and the interactive one.

3.  `make_matrix()` exists because plotly will not accept long data for a heat map; it needs a matrix of values with vectors for the row and column labels. `pivot_wider()` names columns in order of first appearance rather than numerically, which would silently produce a chart with its years out of sequence.

4.  `to_colorscale()` is a three-line adapter converting an R palette into plotly’s \[position, color\] format, so the interactive figure uses the same `mako` palette as the static ones.

```{r Reusable Summary and Plot Functions}

fg_lookup <- draft_groups # swap for read_csv(...) once signed off

master_fg <- master |> left_join(fg_lookup, by = "taxon_key")

# group-filtered summary downstream.
stopifnot(!any(is.na(master_fg$functional_group)))

# Substrate, Turf and Unresolved are excluded from the dropdown
# See notes at the foot of this file for why each one is out
groups <- c("Algae", "Mollusc", "Calcified algae", "Echinoderm",
            "Coral", "Cyanobacteria", "Other invertebrate")


# Summarize one functional group to taxon x year
group_summary <- function(data, group, n_taxa = 12) {
  d <- data |> filter(functional_group == group)

  # Top n taxa within this group, by total cover
  keep <- d |>
    group_by(taxon_key) |>
    summarise(total = sum(percent_cover, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    slice_max(total, n = n_taxa) |>
    pull(taxon_key)

  d |>
    filter(taxon_key %in% keep) |>
    select(all_of(quad_keys), year, taxon_key, percent_cover) |>
    # Completion happens AFTER filtering, so that:
    # 1) Zeros only needed for selected taxa
    # 2) Grid stays small enough
    complete(nesting(!!!syms(c(quad_keys, "year"))), taxon_key,
             fill = list(percent_cover = 0)) |>
    group_by(year, taxon_key) |>
    summarise(mean_cover = mean(percent_cover),
              n_quadrats = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(taxon_key = fct_reorder(taxon_key, mean_cover, .fun = mean))
}


# Plot one group to test functional groups, 
group_heatmap <- function(data, group, n_taxa = 12) {
  d <- group_summary(data, group, n_taxa)

  ggplot(d, aes(x = factor(year), y = taxon_key, fill = mean_cover)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1,
                         labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%"),
                         name = "Mean\ncover") +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(
      title = paste0(group, ": mean percent cover per quadrat"),
      subtitle = paste("Top", n_taxa, "taxa by abundance, pooled across all sites"),
      x = NULL, y = NULL,
      caption = "Point-intercept data, 7,108 quadrats at 41 sites. Absences counted as zero.\nYears 2009-2015 and 2021-2023 not surveyed."
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey45", size = 7.5))
}

# Test it out using one of the functional group classifiers
group_heatmap(master_fg, "Coral")
```

### Exploring by Functional Group

- Grouping to functional level is more robust, because the classification only has to be right about the kind of organism, not the species
- @fig-cover-dropdown lets the reader select a functional group and see its most abundant taxa across the survey years
  - Each group is drawn as its own layer and the dropdown switches between them, so the figure works in a static HTML document with no server behind it
- Substrate is excluded because it was only recorded from 2024 onward and cannot share an axis with groups spanning the full period
- Turf is excluded because it is a single taxon and would render as one row.
- The `Unresolved` entries such as `Unknown Red` and `Brown Crust` is retained in the underlying data but not presented as a result, since it describes the limits of field identification rather than the community.

```{r Interactive Heatmap with Dropdown}
#| label: fig-cover-dropdown
#| fig-cap: "Mean percent cover per quadrat by taxon and survey year, for the most abundant taxa within the selected functional group. Use the dropdown below the plot to switch groups."
#| fig-scap: "Mean percent cover by taxon and year, by functional group"
 
# Plotly cannot filter a heatmap from long data.
# Built ONE TRACE PER GROUP up front, show only the first
# The buttons flip which trace is visible.
# Nothing is recomputed on click, so it works as static HTML


# Build one z-matrix per group: rows = taxa, columns = years.
# Row and column order are set explicitly, because pivot_wider() orders
# columns by first appearance, not numerically.
make_matrix <- function(g) {
  d <- group_summary(master_fg, g)

  # Sorted separately because pivot_wider() names columns by order
  # Here, I sort numerically by year
  yrs <- sort(unique(d$year))

  w <- d |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = taxon_key, names_from = year, values_from = mean_cover) |>
    # taxn_key is a factor order by abundance
    # plotly draws y bottom-up
    # ascending order puts most abundant on top
    arrange(taxon_key) |>                       
    # factor order = ascending abundance
    select(taxon_key, all_of(as.character(yrs)))

  list(
    y = as.character(w$taxon_key), # plotly uses character ≠ factor
    x = as.character(yrs),         
    z = as.matrix(w[, -1]) # drop the label column      
  )
}

# set_names() lets the trace and button loop address groups by name
# as opposed to index, so they are not dropped
mats <- set_names(map(groups, make_matrix), groups)

# Make coloscale in plotly [position, color]
to_colorscale <- function(cols) {
  cols <- substr(cols, 1, 7)          
  # strip alpha - plotly rejects 8-digit hex
  n <- length(cols)
  map(seq_len(n), \(i) list((i - 1) / (n - 1), cols[i]))
}

# rev() because mako runs dark-to-light
# we want dark to represent more cover as opposed to less
mako_scale <- to_colorscale(rev(viridisLite::mako(9)))

# One trace per group; only the first is visible at load
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in groups) {
  m <- mats[[g]]
  p <- add_trace(p,
    z = m$z, x = m$x, y = m$y,
    type = "heatmap",
    colorscale = mako_scale,
    visible = (g == groups[1]),     # only first group drawn at load
    xgap = 1, ygap = 1,             # the white tile borders
    colorbar = list(
      title        = list(text = "Mean<br>cover (%)", side = "top"),
    # <br> no \n: potly title are HTML, so "\n" prints literally
      x            = 1.02,          # just right of the plot area
      xanchor      = "left",
      y            = 1,
      yanchor      = "top",   # top of the bar at the top of the plot
                              # won't wonky with fewer taxa
      len          = 0.75,          # 75% of plot height
      lenmode      = "fraction",
      thickness    = 14,            # pixels wide
      outlinewidth = 0,
      ticksuffix   = "%"
    ),
# <extra></extra> suppreses plotly's default "trace 0" box 
    hovertemplate = "%{y}<br>%{x}<br>%{z:.2f}%<extra></extra>"
  )
}

# One button per group. `groups == g` evaluates to a TRUE/FALSE vector of exactly the right length - one entry per trace, in trace order
# Each button flips the visibility vector and swaps the title
buttons <- map(groups, function(g) {
  list(
    method = "update",
    label  = g,
    args   = list(
      list(visible = groups == g),
      list(title = list(text = paste0(g, ": mean percent cover per quadrat")))
    )
  )
})

cover_dropdown <- p |>
  layout(
    title = list(text = paste0(groups[1], ": mean percent cover per quadrat"),
                 x = 0, xanchor = "left"),
    xaxis = list(side = "top", title = "", type = "category"),
    yaxis = list(title = "", type = "category"),
    height = 560, # fixed, so switching groups doesn't resize
# Bottom margin holds  menu; top  only needs title + year labels
# Margins are load-bearing: plotly doesn't expand for long labels,
# Bars or menus: 
    # Anything outside the plot area needs margin
    # If not, plot gets squeezed to make room.
# l: taxon, r: the colorbar, t: title + year labels, b: the menu
# FIXED: r was 30, too narrow for the colorbar added at x = 1.02
    margin = list(l = 180, r = 30, t = 90, b = 90),
    updatemenus = list(list(
      type        = "dropdown",
      name        = "Functional group:", showarrow = FALSE,
      direction   = "up",         # opens UPWARD, overlaying the plot
      xref        = "paper",      # pos against figure, not the data
      yref        = "paper",
      x           = 1.2,
      xanchor     = "right",      # right edge of figure 
      y           = -0.05,
      yanchor     = "bottom",     # menu hangs below the plot area
      bgcolor     = "white",
      bordercolor = "grey70",
      borderwidth = 1,
      font        = list(size = 9),
      showactive  = TRUE,
      buttons     = buttons
    ))
  )

cover_dropdown
```
